sections.overview: Tramea lacerata is a widely distributed North American skimmer, also recorded on some Caribbean islands and Hawaii.
sections.identification: The dark patches near the body on each hindwing create the “saddlebags” pattern.
sections.habitat: It is associated with ponds and other still or slow waters.
sections.diet: Adults catch flying insects in the air.
sections.behavior: It often glides and is rarely seen perching for long.
sections.reproduction: It breeds in temporary or permanent ponds and ditches; some populations migrate seasonally.
sections.ecology: It is a Tramea like T. onusta; this species has dark hindwing patches, whereas T. onusta has reddish ones.
sections.conservation: The cited Idaho catalog lists a global rank of G5; that broad rank does not resolve local trends.
